text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Malawi Housing Corporation, not required to make profits, has apparently ignored legal advice to wait for parliamentary review and raised rents by 90 percent.
- Voters in seven constituencies in three regions go to the polls on Monday in by-elections to fill vacancies mostly created by the deaths of candidates elected in 1994 general elections.
-Lands and Valuation Minister, Peter Fachi, joined barefooted village chiefs in traditional prayer for good rains and a cure for Aids.
- Malawi's budget management is completely flawed and irrational because it does not address the basics of economic survival for the country, presidential economic advisor Kalonga Stambuli said.
- Two main opposition parties said by-elections in seven constituencies would not be free and fair because of the weakness and incompetence of the Electoral Commission.
- A looming strike at the country's only two sugar manufacturing firms has been postponed after unions said government would try resolve the dispute, centred on allegations of racist expatriates.
